title: connection-quarantine-optimizer-and-deferred-reset-hotfix
author: Asha Kapoor
release_notes: Hotfix: reduce tenant-facing churn from aggressive circuit resets; introduce deferred reset window and probabilistic quarantine smoothing. Backported to patch channel.
description:
Motivation: We observed recurring tenant eviction loops and KV-cache thrash in regional failover scenarios when transient errors caused aggressive circuit resets. The root cause was twofold: (1) immediate hard ejection of connections on transient health flaps, and (2) synchronized reset attempts across nodes that re-triggered the same failure window. This PR introduces a conservative, backwards-compatible hotfix that smooths connection quarantine behavior and defers hard resets to reduce oscillation and KV cache loss.

What this changes (summary):
- Add a deferred-reset window (configurable per-region) that delays final hard eviction to allow transient recoveries to succeed.
- Introduce a probabilistic ejection sanitizer: for soft health flaps we probabilistically stagger quarantine expiry across the cohort to avoid thundering resets.
- Telemetry sanity gating: new metrics and a histogram for deferred-reset duration to detect regressions; added a guard that prevents deferred-reset from triggering if KV-sync lag > configured threshold.
- Canary rollout helpers: a small feature-flag gate and activity log entry so SRE can pin the behavior to a subset of nodes and monitor regressions.
- Tests & observability: unit tests for the backoff calculation, integration test that simulates rapid flap + regional failover, dashboards added for the new metrics.

Checklist:
- [x] Implement deferred-reset + probabilistic staggering
- [x] Add telemetry + dashboards (SLO impact panel)
- [x] Add unit/integration tests and load test script for regional scenario
- [x] Canary rollout flag and rollout doc in /docs/ops/quarantine-rollout.md
- [x] Backport to release/2026-03 patch channel

Risk / mitigation: low-to-moderate. The change is defensive: it reduces the aggressiveness of eviction and adds telemetry to detect negative side effects. We ship behind a feature flag and rolled out to 10% of regional capacity during the canary window. If deferred-reset causes resource pinch we included an emergency kill-switch that reverts to previous behavior immediately.

Related: Linear ENG-1289 for follow-up that tunes default windows by workload; SUP-3112 contains customer-facing incident notes.

Notes and links: implementation borrows the probabilistic staggering idea from RFC-2020 in the runtime proposals doc (internal link: https://linear.app/redwood/ENG-1289/runtime-quarantine-rfc). Rollout playbook: /docs/ops/quarantine-rollout.md (added at end of PR).

Detailed change log (single-string description required by agents): This single PR implements the deferred-reset controller and the ejection sanitizer; it touches the serving runtime quarantine manager, the regional failover coordinator, adds telemetry collectors in the metrics package, updates the feature-flag config, and includes tests and docs. See files_changed for exact locations.
